passage:
The science club built a small weather station on the school roof. It measured temperature, rainfall, and wind direction.
Every morning, club members recorded the numbers and posted them near the office. At first, few students cared.
Then one week, heavy rain was expected. Students began checking the station to see how much rain had fallen. The numbers helped the PE teacher decide whether the field was safe.
The club also compared their records with weather reports online. Sometimes they were different because the school had its own local conditions.
Students learned that weather is not only something on a phone screen. It can be measured, watched, and understood from the place where you stand.
